evidence.text: In September the Century transaction grew from a $68M stalking-horse bid for 71% (1 Jul) to a $91M winning auction bid (3 Sep), then to a whole-company merger ($70M cash plus 1,232,657 shares, ~$137.3M, signed 16 Sep) with KBW and Nelson Mullins as advisors. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 miss came partly on elevated expense (M&A consulting plus IT remediation, $11.9M against $9.7M a year earlier): -2.51%.
evidence.why_not_priced: No estimate source shows a Q3 merger-cost line. If two analysts had raised their expense lines after 16 Sep, the consensus would have drifted down from the ~$1.04 Q2 level, and it has not. It is small because bank investors usually adjust deal costs out, and success fees typically land at closing (Nov), not in Q3.
evidence.independence: Auction 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1746129/000114036126036192/ef20081805_8k.htm (price raised to $88.96M net). The deal itself is the same fact family as the deal-approval finding, but the two land on different lines: Q3 cost here, forward guide there.

evidence.text: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep 2026, the first hike since 2023. Bank7's CFO said on the Q2 call that a hike 'we would benefit from... from an asset sensitive perspective' (deposit cost 2.28-2.30%, about $220M cash). The Q3 call's Q4 NIM outlook could therefore come above the 4.45-4.53% core range.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior: on recent calls management guided NIM down (Q2 NIM 4.81% vs 4.96%) and the Q2 print fell 2.51%. There is no history of a NIM raise to compare against.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the hike was a near coin flip beforehand (~50-57% odds) and is a macro fact every bank holder sees. The company-specific part, the size of a NIM raise at a ~4.5% core-NIM, asset-sensitive bank, is not quantified anywhere public. If it were priced, BSVN would have moved after 16 Sep; the stock sat near the $54.57 10-day average.
evidence.independence: This is a macro-to-company proxy: the company described its asset sensitivity in the Q2 call summary https://www.webull.com.au/news-detail/15277049858696192, but has not confirmed a number since the hike. The hike itself is single-sourced through secondary outlets (see the search results).

evidence.text: On 9 Oct Bank7 filed an 8-K: Century shareholders approved the merger, the Federal Reserve and the New Mexico FID gave approval or non-objection, and closing is expected 'on or about November 1, 2026'. The Q3 call is therefore the first chance for management to firm pro-forma 2027 numbers. The deal deck already showed 25%+ EPS accretion, ~11% TBV dilution, a 1.7-year earnback and 6.3x P/E with synergies.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior deal of this scale (it nearly doubles assets to ~$3.3B). The stock barely moved on the 17 Sep merger announcement (10-day average $54.57 before it, $55.00 now).
evidence.why_not_priced: The accretion numbers are public, and the stock's lack of reaction says the market is either sceptical or has not done the work. Faster-than-expected approvals (closing about 6 weeks after signing) remove timing risk. Detail on purchase-accounting marks against Century's ~3.75% cost of funds could swing the reception either way.
evidence.independence: Merger deck https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1746129/000114036126036855/ef20081983_ex99-2.htm. It is the same transaction as the merger-cost finding, which is sized on the Q3 cost line, not the forward guide.

evidence.text: On the Q2 call management flagged 'significant loan pay downs' to overcome in H2, with Q3 fundings expected at about double Q2 and mid-single-digit full-year loan growth. That risks a flat or lower loan balance, partly offset by prepayment-fee income.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, with loans down slightly on the half year: -2.51%. That move came mainly on the EPS miss.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is inside what management warned of, so mostly priced. The open question is whether fundings matched the 'double' claim, which nothing public measures.

evidence.text: US long-steel and rebar selling prices were 'steady to down' through July on low seasonal demand, bearish sentiment and more Gulf Coast imports, per SteelOrbis weekly headlines (2, 16, 23 and 30 July). ChemAnalyst had rebar -0.94% in the week to 2026-08-07 and flat thereafter. Firming only came from late August and September. Management guided half of NASG's +$40m q/q to 'volume growth and margin expansion' and admitted on the call to market discounting it would not match. Soft July pricing and demand put that half of the bridge (~$20m, about $0.14/share) at risk, either as lost volume or lower realisations.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same line as Q3 FY26: there, shipments fell to 750kt (from 798kt) and the stock still rose +3.94%. A market pricing a volume or price shortfall would show consensus clearly under the guide-implied ~$2.05 and a lower revenue bar than $2.54-2.57B. It does not. The 133%-wide option spread means the skew cannot tell us whether this is hedged. The effect is netted against finding 1 (lower scrap): the spread is what matters, so this is the price side only.
evidence.independence: ChemAnalyst, 2026-08-20 (https://www.chemanalyst.com/NewsAndDeals/NewsDetails/us-steel-rebar-prices-stay-range-bound-as-buyers-adopt-44010): rebar -0.94% on Aug 7 then flat, July +0.96% m/m, 'increased import availability', 'comfortable distributor inventories'. What the money buys: the cash leg of a deal management calls 'broadly neutral to minimally dilutive' to core FFO in year one, so it is a small negative or zero, not distress.

If the overhang were cleared, the stock would trade back toward its pre-deal ~$144 (the 2026-08-03 close in the prospectus) rather than $133. evidence.independence: Deal terms and accretion language: Prologis release (https://ir.prologis.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1049/prologis-announces-recommended-acquisition-of-segro-plc); the Q2 call's refusal to discuss it is in the transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15238046746764288).

evidence.text: On the Q1 FY27 call (Jul 16) management said some large-deal decisions 'have actually slipped to quarter two', the pipeline is 'healthy', BFSI client insourcing 'is behind us' and BFSI Americas is ramping. evidence.independence: Same company document as the guide in the bar. HCLTech's +27% bookings is a separate peer signal that deal flow was live in the quarter (https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/hcltech-q2-fy27-results-revenue-profit-and-deal-wins/).
